children: Arabica coffee futures on ICE steadied on Monday after hitting a fresh 10 week low on looming increases in certified stocks and rains in top grower Brazil.
Raw sugar and cocoa also edged up meanwhile.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
edged up 0.2% to $2.8630 per lb at 1223 GMT, having set a fresh 10-week-low of $2.8150.
* Exchange data showed nearly 65,000 bags of arabica (KC-TOT-PENDING) are pending grading or quality controls so they can be certified as deliverable against ICE contracts.

* Dealers, brokers and analysts told Reuters last week that traders are planning, over the next couple of months, to deliver at least 300,000 bags of arabica to ICE exchange warehouses, where stocks have sunk to 26-year lows.
* A broker said the potential for rising stocks plus flowering in Brazil thanks to the rains is putting arabica under pressure overall.
* Robusta coffee
fell 0.4% to $3,513 a ton, having posted a 3% gain last week.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 1% to 18.32 cents per lb, heading back near last week's 16-month peak of 18.88.
* The U.S. Department of Agriculture has cut its 2026/27 sugar production forecast to 8.84 million short tons (ST), the smallest volume since 2019/20.

* Elsewhere, sugar remains underpinned by looming supply tightness in India, Thailand and Europe, as well as strength in energy markets, which can encourage more use of cane to make the biofuel ethanol rather than sugar.
* Oil prices rose on Monday, remaining above $100 a barrel as the U.S.-Iran war put more Gulf oil supplies out of reach.
* White sugar
rose 0.9% to $527.60 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​​rose 1.1% to £4,378 per ton, having lost 4% last week.

* "Two risks sit outside the current price. EUDR compliance (struggles) and a stronger Harmattan. For now the market is willing to look past all of it and trade decent short-term availability instead," said commodity intelligence firm Vesper.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.8% to $6,011 a ton, having lost 4% last week.
